seoTitle: Obstacles & Soil Load: 5 Factors Raising Marble & Terrazzo Honing Bids
metaDescription: Obstacles, soil load, furniture moves, and security escorts can raise marble terrazzo honing quotes 15%-45%. See the math and compare bids in our Quote Comparator.
excerpt: Two lobbies of the same size can receive stone honing quotes thousands of dollars apart because of site conditions. Learn the five factors that push marble and terrazzo estimates up 15%-45% and the practical steps that remove most of that premium.
quickAnswer: Furniture and planter moves, heavy soil load or old coatings, after-hours security escorts, restricted access and water management, and edge-heavy layouts are the five site factors that raise lobby marble and terrazzo honing quotes by 15%-45%. A lobby that would price at $3.00 per sq ft on a clear, lightly soiled floor can easily reach $3.90-$4.35 once these conditions stack up.

blocks.text: Why Site Conditions Matter More Than Square Footage

Stone vendors price from a clear-floor baseline: an empty, lightly soiled marble or terrazzo field with open access, a nearby water source, and an eight-hour work window. Every deviation from that baseline costs crew time, and crew time at $55-$95 per technician hour is the bulk of every honing estimate. When a vendor walks your lobby, they are effectively scoring the five conditions below. Knowing them lets you fix what you can before the walkthrough and challenge padding where conditions do not justify it.

blocks.text: Factor 1: Furniture, Planters, and Lobby Fixtures

Stone planters can weigh 300-800 lb with soil, and moving them safely requires a pallet jack, floor protection, and two or three people. Lounge seating, security desks, digital directories, and stanchion lines all add minutes. Vendors usually estimate 15-30 minutes of two-person labor per large item. A lobby with 12 heavy items can add four to six labor hours, or $440-$1,140 at specialty rates, before honing starts.
Factor 2: Soil Load and Old Coatings

Ground-in soil in walk lanes and yellowed acrylic or urethane finish on terrazzo add stripping and coarse grit passes. A floor needing a coating strip plus a 100 or 200 grit start can add $1.00-$2.00 per sq ft. Soil load is also a daily cleaning issue: lobbies near parking garages or construction sites carry more abrasive grit. Specifying neutral chemistry from the start, such as a 1:256 neutral pH quaternary like Diversey Virex II 256 for daily disinfecting needs or a Safer Choice plant-based cleaner such as ECOS Pro Orange Plus diluted for routine soil, helps avoid residue buildup that later costs money to cut through. Always confirm with your stone vendor that daily products are stone-safe at the specified dilution.

blocks.title: Check dilution, not just the label
blocks.text: Even neutral cleaners can leave residue films on polished stone when over-concentrated. Residue attracts soil and dulls gloss, which accelerates the need for honing. Require dilution control equipment and document ratios in the janitorial scope.
Factor 3: After-Hours Security and Work Windows

Class A towers and government buildings often require a paid security escort for contractors after 10 p.m., badge pre-registration, or background checks. If escort time is billed back at $35-$60 per hour, a ten-night project adds $2,800-$4,800. Narrow windows, for example 11 p.m. to 5 a.m. with a mandatory one-hour sealer cure before opening, cut productive time and spread the job over more nights, each with its own setup and teardown.
Factors 4 and 5: Access, Utilities, and Layout

Planetary machines and wet vacuums need water, drainage for slurry, and sometimes 220V power. If the nearest janitor sink is two floors away or loading dock access requires a freight elevator reservation, vendors add hauling time. Layout matters too: columns, brass divider strips, medallion inlays, and long perimeter edges must be hand-worked with smaller edgers, which run at a fraction of open-field productivity. A 2,000 sq ft lobby with eight columns and a border inlay can carry as much edge work as a 4,000 sq ft open rectangle.

items: Confirm the location of water, floor drains, and power on a marked floor plan before the walkthrough.
Reserve the freight elevator and loading dock for the vendor's trailer unload in advance.
Have building engineers remove or relocate planters and lobby furniture the afternoon before work begins.
Issue contractor credentials ahead of time so escorts are only needed for initial check-in.
Provide accurate CAD drawings showing inlays, columns, and borders so edge work is not guessed high.

Relocate touchless towel dispensers or other wall fixtures near the floor edge only if they obstruct edging; units like the Georgia-Pacific enMotion 10-inch dispenser are wall-mounted at ADA depth and typically stay put.

blocks.text: Pre-Bid Checklist to Cut the Premium

items.name: Document conditions
items.text: Photograph the floor, coatings, soil lanes, and every obstacle so all bidders price the same conditions.

items.name: Clear the floor
items.text: Commit in the RFP to having the building move furniture so vendors do not price it.

items.name: Publish work windows
items.text: State exact nightly hours, escort requirements, and weekend availability to allow longer shifts.

items.name: Confirm utilities
items.text: List water, drain, and power locations and any freight elevator limits.

items.name: Request itemized premiums
items.text: Ask bidders to show the baseline rate and each condition premium separately.

faqs.a: Yes, when several conditions stack: heavy soil with an old urethane coating, a dozen stone planters, a 1 a.m. to 5 a.m. window with paid escorts, and an inlay-heavy layout. In those cases, the extra nights and coarse grit passes are real. Ask for itemization to confirm each premium is tied to a documented condition.

faqs.q: Who should move furniture, the building or the vendor?
faqs.a: If your building engineers or day porters can safely move items, doing it in-house usually saves 5%-12%. If the vendor moves items, require that they carry adequate general liability, name the owner and manager as additional insureds on the certificate of insurance, and photograph item condition beforehand.

It can. Wet honing slurry contains fine stone and diamond residue and should not be dumped down drains without filtration under many local codes. Vendors may add $75-$250 per job for slurry collection and disposal, more if the site lacks a suitable drain or requires hauling offsite.

faqs.q: Do safety requirements add cost on terrazzo?
faqs.a: Cement terrazzo contains silica, and grinding falls under OSHA's respirable crystalline silica standard, which favors wet methods or vacuum dust collection. Vendors that follow compliant methods may price slightly higher, but that cost protects occupants and your liability. Also ask for HazCom-compliant SDS for sealers and strippers.

faqs.q: Can better daily cleaning lower future honing quotes?
faqs.a: Definitely. Deeper walk-off matting, nightly dust mopping, and residue-free neutral cleaning reduce soil load, which is the factor most likely to add coarse grit passes. Many buildings cut their next restoration quote by 10%-20% after one year of improved daily care.
